rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (score 680.6) and iteration 4 (669.9) both finish the oval and s-bend, but the slalom fails in all 20 trials per iteration. Progress rose from 0.35 to 0.42 when the sensor spread went from ±0.04 to ±0.05 m and kp dropped to 1.0. Max error is still about 0.063 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit, and the slalom loses the line about once per run. Body width cannot widen that limit (it would need body_width above 0.19 m, out of range), so the robot has to keep the tape under its sensors. Line loss happens when the summed reading falls below 0.05, which means no sensor covers any tape. Two changes address this. (1) Use 7 sensors at x = -0.06, -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06 m, spanning the full body width, so one sensor is always near the tape at the sharpest bends. (2) Enlarge the sensor footprint from 12 mm to 16 mm, so a sensor still sees tape at about 2 cm off-centre (the tape is 25 mm wide and half-width is 12.5 mm plus half the sensor). Weights are set to about 40 per metre of offset, clipped to ±2: [-2, -1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6, 2]. This keeps the steering gain per metre close to the iteration-4 value, so kp 1.0 and kd 0.8 are kept. Speed (1.0), ki (0.02), line_loss (last_direction) and the drivetrain are held fixed so the sensing change can be read. Expected result: fewer slalom line-loss events, slalom progress above 0.5, and the oval and s-bend still completing at about 2.0 to 2.4 s. Risks: the larger footprint may raise steering jitter on straights, and 7 sensors add a little more noise averaging. Hypotheses: (a) slalom failures come from losing the line at the sharpest bends because outer sensors do not reach far enough, so wider and larger-footprint sensing fixes most of it; (b) the remaining slalom error is set by lag at this speed. Measurements wanted: per-track progress, max_error and line_loss_events to see whether the first failing slalom bend is passed, and steering_oscillation to check the jitter cost of the larger footprint. If the slalom still loses the line, the next step is to test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right', or to lower base_speed to about 0.9.
